messages:
incident-bot: Pager alert: high NotReady count in infer-usw1 zone affecting inference pools (kubelet restarts + pod crashes). Auto-escalation to oncall.
maya-oncall: seeing it, joining. Are we seeing customer errors or just internal evictions?
devon: quick look at kubelet logs shows repeated container OOMs + CUDA driver errors on a subset of nodes. snippet: 
```
May 04 11:08:23 node-42 kubelet: container runtime stderr: cuda_driver: failed to allocate device memory: out of memory
May 04 11:08:24 node-42 kubelet: kubelet: kubelet runtime crashloop, restarting container
```
ryan: ok -- first step: cordon the most-reported nodes and drain gracefully. Add more replicas for the serving deployment to reduce per-node pressure.
olga: cordoned node-42 and node-43 (those show repeated kubelet restarts). Draining now with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data. Command run: `kubectl drain node-42 node-43 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
maya-oncall: redirecting traffic: enabling failover routing to infer-eu1 for customers on high-sla routes. Triggered fallback policy.
devon: runtime logs also show host kernel OOM messages preceding driver failures; suspect memory leak in recent runtime image (runtimes/image:v2.8.1).
ryan: rollback suggestion: pin pool to v2.8.0 temporarily and restart pods on healthy nodes; that should remove the leak while we investigate.
eng-runtime: got the ping, will validate crash signature. If it's the v2.8.1 allocator change, we should hotfix tomorrow.
olga: applied a temporary HPA bump on serving-deploy to scale from 6 -> 12 replicas to spread load while nodes recover. `kubectl apply -f hpa-temp-bump.yaml`
infra-bot: deployment bot: new rollout started for serving-deploy -> image pinned to runtimes/image:v2.8.0 across infer-usw1. Canary: 2 pods.
maya-oncall: customer impact: initial spike caused ~1200 failed requests over 12m; error rate back down to normal on retried traffic after routing change. Notifying support for top-3 impacted customers.
devon: collecting heap dumps from crashed containers and kernel dmesg from affected nodes. Uploading to /tmp/incident-62745/ for postmortem.
ryan: handoff: @eng-runtime take primary ownership for root cause and remediation. Oncall remains watching for 30m then close if stable.
eng-runtime: acknowledged, will run repro + memory profiler. Tentative root cause tracked as allocator change in v2.8.1 interacting with certain CUDA driver versions.
maya-oncall: notes: create incident ticket, severity S2, include customers impacted and timelines. Follow-up: schedule a coordinated rollout with canary metrics tightened and kernel/cuda version gating. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: node-42 rebooted by node-autorecover; kubelet came back, pods rescheduled. Current status: infer-usw1 node readiness 98%, serving pods stable.
maya-oncall: closing handoff. Monitoring window 30m. Good job team, file postmortem and link to ticket.
